original_question: Compute the invariant ms([0, 1], r), the largest guaranteed Lebesgue measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of the unit interval [0, 1], at least in the case r = 2.
target_in_paper: §8, Problem 8.3: calculate ms([0,1], r), at least for r = 2.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s main target very closely: it identifies the correct invariant ms([0,1], r), uses the unit interval with Lebesgue measure, quantifies over measurable r-colorings, asks for a guaranteed monochromatic symmetric measurable subset, and singles out the case r = 2, which is exactly the special case emphasized in §8.
missing_details: The admissible symmetries are central symmetries of the ambient real line, i.e. reflections x ↦ c − x for some c ∈ R; equivalently, a subset B ⊆ [0,1] is symmetric iff B = c − B for some real c.

Formally, ms([0,1], r) is an infimum over measurable r-colorings χ, not just an informal 'largest guaranteed measure': ms([0,1], r) = inf_χ max_{1≤i≤r} sup{λ(B): B ⊆ χ^{-1}(i), B measurable, and B = c − B for some c ∈ R}.
The parameter r is a finite integer (the survey treats finite colorings; in this context one usually takes r ≥ 2).

To be fully paper-faithful, the question should stay with Problem 8.3 itself and not drift into the separate asymptotic problem for the constant c in ms([0,1], r) ~ c/r^2, which the survey isolates as Problem 8.4.

An equivalent discrete formulation is available in the paper’s surrounding discussion: the interval problem can be phrased as determining the limit of the normalized discrete Ramsey quantity MS(n,r)/n.
refined_question:
Calculate the invariant ms([0,1], r), at least for r = 2, where [0,1] is endowed with Lebesgue measure and admissible symmetries are the central reflections x ↦ c − x of the real line; equivalently, determine
ms([0,1], r) = inf_{χ:[0,1]→{1,…,r} measurable} max_{1≤i≤r} sup{λ(B) : B ⊆ χ^{-1}(i), B is measurable, and B = c − B for some c ∈ R}.
In particular, determine ms([0,1], 2).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine lim_{n→∞} MS(n,r)/n, at least for r = 2, where MS(n,r) = min_{χ:[n]→[r]} max_{1≤i≤r} max{|B| : B ⊆ χ^{-1}(i) and B = g − B for some g ∈ Z}.
justification: The draft is essentially aiming at the survey’s §8 interval problem. In §8 the authors introduce the discrete interval quantity MS(n,r), say that its normalized limit exists, and identify the corresponding continuous invariant on [0,1] as the least upper bound of ε such that every measurable r-coloring of [0,1] contains a monochromatic symmetric subset of Lebesgue measure ε. They then state Problem 8.3 asking to calculate this value, at least for r = 2. The general meaning of the notation ms is supplied earlier in §5, where ms is defined as the maximal guaranteed measure of a monochromatic symmetric subset for measurable colorings of compact objects. The survey also treats the asymptotic constant c in ms([0,1], r) ~ c/r^2 as a different problem (Problem 8.4), so the refined question should remain focused on the exact interval invariant itself rather than broaden to asymptotics.
